content:
Apple's September launch event is just around the corner, where three new iPhone models are expected to debut: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Ultra. Here's a sneak peek.

iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will succeed the widely popular 17 Pro lineup.

Rumoured new features include:

  • Powered by the A20 Pro chip, delivering improved performance and better power efficiency
  • Major camera upgrades, notably a variable aperture added to the main lens
  • Dynamic Island shrunk by 35%, for a sleeker design
  • New colour options, headlined by a bold Burgundy
  • The longest battery life ever, with the iPhone 18 Pro Max seeing especially significant gains
  • Redesigned Camera Control button
  • Apple's in-house C2 modem
  • New satellite connectivity features, including 5G support

The starting price of the iPhone 18 Pro is also expected to rise. External estimates put it at US$1,399, but I reckon it'll be closer to US$1,199 or US$1,249.

iPhone Ultra

The iPhone Ultra is rumoured to be the name of Apple's first foldable phone, with a price tag north of US$2,000, carving out an entirely new premium market.

Its foldable design makes the iPhone Ultra Apple's most groundbreaking model to date. It adopts a wide book-style fold, with an outer display of around 5.4 inches and an inner display of 7.8 inches — much like an iPad mini.

The build is expected to match the iPhone Air, featuring a titanium frame for a sleek, refined look.

The iPhone Ultra will sport two rear cameras (main and ultra-wide) plus two front cameras — one for each display. Biometric authentication will switch from Face ID to Touch ID.

The software will be the biggest highlight: iOS 27 will support side-by-side multitasking and adaptive landscape layouts, perfectly suited to the new form factor.

Performance is expected to be on par with the iPhone 18 Pro, also powered by the A20 Pro chip, with a vapour chamber and the C2 modem on board.

The missing models: iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2

Typically, the September event also sees the launch of a new entry-level iPhone 18 and the successor to the iPhone Air.

However, reports suggest Apple is giving its autumn lineup a major shake-up this year, pushing the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 back to early 2027.

It's unclear whether this is a purely strategic move or one forced by current memory chip supply constraints. Either way, the absence of cheaper models means this autumn's new iPhone lineup will focus exclusively on the premium end of the market.

Planning to upgrade your iPhone this autumn? Which model will you go for? Let us know in the comments.
